bottleneck: Bacteria constantly trade DNA through conjugation, transformation, and transduction, meaning engineered genes can escape into wild populations regardless of design intent. Antibiotic-resistance markers and synthetic constructs have already been observed moving in the wild, and engineered traits that confer advantage will spread by selection. No genetic isolation mechanism has survived contact with real microbial ecology, where billions of transfer events occur continuously.
current_state: Researchers test genetic firewalls like recoded genomes and synthetic amino acids, but horizontal transfer of engineered DNA remains an unsolved risk in any open application. Containment is theoretical.
title: Horizontal gene transfer escapes engineered designs
why_it_blocks: Gene flow ignores engineering boundaries. Until transfer can be prevented or rendered harmless, every environmental release gambles with the global microbial gene pool, and the stakes include spreading engineered traits irreversibly.
